newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament rejects bid for confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament rejects bid for confidence vote.

text.p: Turkey's parliament on Wednesday rejected a bid by the secularist opposition to force a confidence vote in Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan over his Islamist foreign policy.
Turk parliament rejects bid for confidence vote
Deputies voted by 275 to 256 not to hold a confidence vote, over Erbakan's controversial trip 10 days ago to Libya -- the target of Western anger for alleged support of terrorism.
"Placing the censure motion on the agenda has not been accepted," Uluc Gurkan, acting speaker, told the parliament after a secret ballot.
The vote followed almost six hours of often tense debate, with opposition and government MPs trading charges and insults.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, has angered his secularist critics and alienated NATO-ally the United States with an effort to turn Ankara from the West and toward the Arab and Moslem world.
